Case study · Broadband availability · GIS

California, connected?

A location-by-location look at high-speed internet in all 58 California counties, built from the public Broadband Data Collection (BDC) of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). Where are the gaps, why do they look so different from county to county, and which technologies reach the last locations?

    05

    Method & data

    Built from public files only. No coordinates or addresses from the FCC's Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric are used or shown.

    Definitions

    Status thresholds (all lenses)

    Served≥100/20 Mbps on a counted technology, with low latency (≤100 ms)
    Underserved≥25/3 Mbps but <100/20 Mbps on a counted technology, with low latency
    Unserved<25/3 Mbps, or no counted technology

    Mbps = megabits per second, download/upload. Speeds are maximum advertised speeds. A location takes the best qualifying offer from any provider.

    Lenses: policy basis

    Any technologyFull technology-neutral view: every reported technology counts.
    BEAD 2025NTIA BEAD Restructuring Policy Notice, June 6, 2025. Adds unlicensed fixed wireless as existing service; upper bound, because provider evidence was required.
    BEAD 2022NTIA BEAD Notice of Funding Opportunity, 2022 ("reliable broadband service"), as FCC technology codes 10, 40, 50, 71, 72.
    Fiber + cableWired-only view.
    Fiber onlyFiber-only view.

    Technologies by lens

    ✓ = counted as existing service under the lens. * GSO satellite is counted under Any technology, but none of its records qualify: none advertise 100/20 and all report high latency. Offered = share of all California locations where the technology is reported at any speed; ≥100/20 = reported at 100/20 Mbps or faster, before the latency condition. One location can have several technologies.

    Data & processing

    • FCC National Broadband Map, California fixed broadband availability, all technologies, as of June 30, 2026: 88,973,679 rows, one per location, provider and technology.
    • Loaded into DuckDB and collapsed to 10,289,142 locations (one record per location ID).
    • County and tract from the 2020 census block geographic identifier (GEOID) of each location; the first five digits are the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) county code.
    • Aggregated to H3 cells at resolution 6 (statewide map) and 8 (county maps).
    • Urban/rural shares come from the FCC county summary and are based on housing units, independent of the lens.

    Checks & caveats

    • Reconciliation. All 10,289,142 location IDs join 1:1 to the FCC served/unserved file, with identical county assignment. Recomputing the FCC's three flags at ≥100/20 Mbps with no latency condition reproduces them exactly: any technology; terrestrial (all non-satellite codes); and wired (copper, cable, fiber).
    • Latency. Every lens also requires the provider-reported low-latency flag (round-trip latency of 100 milliseconds or less). This removes 783 locations from the FCC terrestrial count and 1,700 from the wired count. All 30.9 million geostationary satellite rows report high latency. Every LEO row reports ≥100/20 with low latency.
    • Advertised, not measured. Speeds and the latency flag are provider-reported maximum advertised values, not measured throughput. A location can contain several units.
    • Geography. H3 cells that cross a county line are kept once per county. The lowest-served tract lists skip tracts with fewer than 25 locations. Boundaries are Census 1:500,000 cartographic files, simplified for display.
    • BEAD 2025 counts every reported unlicensed fixed wireless offer. It does not test the provider evidence that states required, so it is an upper bound.

    Sources

    • FCC National Broadband Map: data download. Fixed availability by technology, served/unserved file and summary by geography, June 30, 2026 filing (released Nov 10, 2026).
    • FCC Broadband Data Collection
    • NTIA BEAD Notice of Funding Opportunity (2022)
    • NTIA BEAD Restructuring Policy Notice (2025)
    • U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary files, 2023 (1:500,000). County, state and place boundaries.
    • U.S. Census Bureau city and town population estimates, Vintage 2023. Used to choose the map labels.
    • Natural Earth 1:50m countries (Mexico outline), via world-atlas
    • H3 hexagonal grid, drawn with h3-js (Apache-2.0)
